To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MEA cluster on biodiversity is not as fragmented as it is often assumed to be, that there are a number of institutional and cognitive barriers to EPI among the agreements, but that these are not necessarily insurmountable.

the MEA cluster on biodiversity is characterized by a high degree of institutional interplay, but this does not translate into effective management of interplay, which in turn is constrained by institutional, political and knowledge barriers.
EPI among multilateral environmental treaties is a problem that can only be solved at the national level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the management of institutional interdependence among MEAs.
the question of whether the MEA cluster on biodiversity is moving towards EPI and if so, why.
the question of how to manage the interplay among MEAs in order to enhance EPI in global environmental governance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MEA cluster is a good example of how MEAs can interact and cooperate, and how they can be managed to do so.
EPI among MEA is a complex and challenging issue, and that there is still a long way to go before MEA can achieve the desired level of policy integration.
EPI in MEA clusters is not a problem of institutional structure but of effective management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EPI is a process, not a state.
MEAs are increasingly interacting with one another, and that this is a positive development for the MEA system.
the MEA cluster on biodiversity has been defragmented to an extent where EPI is a matter of institutional interaction management rather than of institutional fragmentation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EPI is not a problem of institutional design but rather of institutional interaction.
EPI in the MEA system should not be understood as a problem of institutional structure, but of institutional management.
MEAs are not the only actors involved in EPI.
